Situation1: You just realized a comment you made has deeply hurt your friend's feelings, and you need to call them right now to apologize and clear the air.
Expectation2: Wash and condition clients' hair before cutting or styling
Situation2: Heavy product buildup is causing tight tangles that will impede scissors.
Story: I stared at my phone, heart pounding, as I watched my next client settle into the salon chair. The memory of my careless comment to Jamie replayed in my mind—her face falling, the awkward silence. I knew I had to call her, to explain, to apologize before the misunderstanding grew roots. But right now, my hands were tangled in someone else’s hair, thick with product and knots. As a hairdresser, I couldn’t skip the wash and conditioning; if I did, the scissors would snag, the cut would be uneven, and my client would leave disappointed. She was already glancing at her watch, expecting me to work my usual magic. My phone buzzed with a message from Jamie, and guilt twisted in my stomach. I felt pulled in two directions—my friend needed honesty and care, my client needed my skill and attention. I gripped the comb, torn, wishing I could be in two places at once.
